claim.statement: Kimera-SWM's Walker step-0 selection rule is documented at takwin.py:30371-30393 (Phase 229.4): among graph nodes whose concept-name is a whole-word token in the lowercased-whitespace-split prompt, pick the one with the maximum string length. Fallback ladder: (1) centroid-closest by embedding cosine, (2) highest-entropy. The rule is purely architectural and length-based — NOT encoder activation, NOT rarity, NOT semantic centrality.
claim.operationalization: For each of 265 full-walk cycles from pg100.txt: (a) reconstruct the source paragraph from paragraph_index; (b) compute the set of whole-word lowercase tokens (whitespace split); (c) filter walk concepts to those whose lowercase is in that set; (d) check that the rule predicts position-0 = the longest such matching concept. Rule holds iff position-0 IS that longest concept.
claim.h0: Position-0 is NOT determined by the longest-prompt-matching-concept rule (would yield <99% match)
claim.h1: Position-0 IS exactly the longest-prompt-matching-concept (would yield ≥99% match)
